chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Jaʿfar, from his father:
That ʿAlī عليه السلام did not consider there to be any harm in the blood of that which has not been slaughtered ritually being on the garment, so a man prays in it—meaning the blood of fish.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: If a dog or a pig touches a person's garment while both are dry, then the place of their touch on it should be sprinkled with water; and if they are wet, then whatever they touched should be washed with water.

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: garment or clothing in which one performs salat (prayer)
key_terms.بِالْمَاءِ: with water, the means of purification mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.خِنْزِيرٌ: pig, whose contact with clothing is discussed in relation to purification
key_terms.دَمَ السَّمَكِ: the blood of fish, specified here as not preventing prayer in the garment
key_terms.رَطْبَيْنِ: wet, indicating a state requiring washing
key_terms.كَلْبٌ: dog, whose contact with clothing is discussed in relation to purification
key_terms.يَابِسَيْنِ: dry, indicating a state affecting the ruling of purification

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fish blood or contact with a dog or pig on clothing for prayer?
ai.summary: This passage addresses rulings of ritual purity concerning blood on clothing and contact with a dog or pig. It states that fish blood does not prevent prayer in a garment, and it distinguishes between dry and wet contact with a dog or pig in determining whether sprinkling or washing is required.
